pages.en:
Dawn is near.

The farther we advance through the forest, the less we speak, and the heavier our silence becomes.

When he emerges from these woods, Shirou Emiya will have to confront that man.

He has no prospect of victory. If they fight, his defeat is certain.

He knows that the moment their swords cross, he will merely be butchered.

I, Emiya Shirou, must fight that man when we get to the castle.
There is no chance of victory, and a certain loss awaits.
I know I’ll just be killed once we start fighting.

“What else could I do?

“No matter what I saved, there were always people left unsaved. No matter how many conflicts I ended, another was born.

“So long as such things exist, a Hero of Justice has no choice but to go on existing.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It can’t be helped, right?
No matter who I save, there are always people who will perish. No matter how many conflicts I resolve, new conflicts are always created.
A superhero has to keep existing as long as conflict exists.”

pages.en:
“And so I killed.

“To save one person, I trampled the wishes of dozens. Then, to save those I had trampled, I cast aside the wishes of even more.

“I murdered salvation for dozens, preserved only what I could see before me, and killed still more hopes.

“Each time I told myself this would be the end. This time, no one would have to grieve. I persisted in that paltry stubbornness.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That’s why I killed.
I trampled on dozens of wishes to save one person. I ignored even more people to save those I trampled over.
I killed scores of people, rescued only those in front of me, and destroyed many more wishes.
I kept being stubborn, saying that it will end this time, that everyone would become happy.”

“So long as I lived, conflict met my eyes wherever I went.

“There was no end to it. I never dreamed of a world without conflict.

“All I wanted was that, at least within the world I could know, no one should have to weep.”

“But it never ended.
Conflicts come into my view as long as I’m alive.
It was endless. I didn’t dream of a world without conflicts.
I just wanted people in my view not to cry.”

“Because everyone present cannot be saved, someone must inevitably be sacrificed.

“——And so——

“To minimize the harm, I cut away those destined to be left out with my own hands—swiftly, even one second sooner.

“That is the course proper to a hero, to the Hero of Justice that man believed his ideal.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes, the seats are limited. There are always fewer seats called happiness than there are people to fill them.
Since you cannot save everyone, someone will have to be sacrificed.
And…
I quickly killed the ones that would eventually fall out to minimize the damage.
This is what it means to be that boy’s vision of the ideal superhero.”

“Even so, if I could save someone, that was enough.

“The Shirou Emiya of that time had failed to keep his vow.

“Then——if becoming a Guardian allowed me to play some part in preventing this so-called extinction of humanity, I believed that would be enough.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But I did not care, so long as I could save people.
Emiya Shirou could not fulfill his oath.
SoI thought it would be fine if I could become a guardian to take part in stopping humanity’s destruction.”

“They do not save people. They simply erase, without distinction between good and evil, those who would bring harm to the world.

“They do not rescue those weeping in despair. They are slaughterers who eliminate the despairing in order to save outsiders living happily beyond the reach of that despair.

“——It is absurd. How is that any different from what *I* had always done?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“They do not save people. All they do is eliminate harmful people, without distinction of good or evil.
They do not save people in despair. Instead, they eliminate people in despair in order to save others who are enjoying life.
It’s so ridiculous. How am I different from before?”

His own strength had been unequal to the task, so he entrusted himself to a greater power.

But what awaited him was ultimately the same.

He believed that power could realize what he could not——only to discover that it had merely magnified everything he himself had done.

There was just more despair.
He relied on a greater power since his powers alone were not enough.
But it ended up being the same.
He thought the power would make his wish come true, but it only made him do the same things on a greater scale.

“…Archer. All this time, you have been——”

“I grew accustomed to that as well. Humanity repeats itself. In every age, the strong strip the weak of everything they possess. And I was taught that this was the most efficient form of prosperity.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Archer. You have repeated such a thing forever…?”
“I got used to it. Humans repeat things. The strong feed on the weak, regardless of what age we’re talking about. And I came to realize that it is the most efficient way to prosper.”

He became a hero with only one thought: that he would save as many people as possible.

And in the end——did he fail to realize that wish even once?

“Save as many people as possible”.
The man became a hero with that one wishbut in the end, he could not make it come true even once.

But I staked everything on it. I could not contain myself unless I believed in it. While I acted as a guardian, this was the one hope that kept me going.”
